extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, USPTO OED staff, and counsel handling USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.25, including what kinds of factual disputes will preclude decision on the documentary record and related procedural obligations during limited recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentary-record disposition standard for interim suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b), a request for interim suspension shall be heard by the USPTO Director on the documentary record unless the practitioner's response establishes a genuine issue of material fact as to specified matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may decide the request based on the written record unless one of the specific genuine-issue grounds (see separate entries) is established. The Final Order applies that standard to determine whether interim suspension is appropriate on the written record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine issue: crime did not constitute a serious crime
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner can preclude a documentary-record decision only by establishing a genuine issue of material fact that 'the crime did not constitute a serious crime.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of the narrow factual disputes identified in 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(3) that, if credibly raised, requires further proceedings beyond the documentary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine issue: practitioner is not the person who committed the crime
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner can preclude a documentary-record decision only by establishing a genuine issue of material fact that 'the practitioner is not the person who committed the crime.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identity of the convicted person is an explicitly enumerated ground under 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(3); a credible dispute on this point requires further factfinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine issue: conviction deprived practitioner of due process
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner can preclude a documentary-record decision only by establishing a genuine issue of material fact that 'the conviction was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute a deprivation of due process.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A showing that the underlying criminal conviction violated fundamental procedural protections is the third narrow ground in §11.25(b)(3) requiring additional proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters that do not preclude documentary decision under §11.25(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Remorse, financial hardship, and post-conviction rehabilitation are not genuine issues of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b) that would preclude an interim suspension decision on the written record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly rejects these matters as bases for avoiding an interim suspension on documentary review: 'Respondent's remorse, the financial impact of the interim suspension, and the Respondent's rehabilitation are not the genuine issues of material fact precluding a decision on the written record under 37 C.F.R. §11.25(b).'

rubrics_metrics.name: Responses to the disciplinary complaint are distinct from documentary-record challenges
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments that respond to the disciplinary complaint itself (e.g., disputing factual counts in the Complaint) do not necessarily constitute grounds to contest the imposition of an interim suspension on the written record under 37 C.F.R. §11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order notes that a response disputing counts in the Complaint is 'a response to the disciplinary Complaint itself, not the proposed imposition of an interim suspension on the written record,' and thus is not a permissible basis to defeat a documentary-record interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for waiver/suspension of regulations (37 C.F.R. §11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 C.F.R. §11.3, 'In an extraordinary situation, when justice requires, any requirement of the regulations of this part ... may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order applies this standard and holds there is 'no extraordinary situation justifying a waiver of the interim suspension regulation'—noting that remorse, financial impact, and rehabilitation do not meet the 'extraordinary' threshold for waiver under §11.3(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client business and withdrawal obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice for 30 days to wind up client business before the Office and is directed to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. §10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During the limited-recognition period the practitioner must (1) wind up all client matters before the Office, (2) withdraw per §10.40, and (3) not accept new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new USPTO clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an express restriction tied to the limited-recognition period to protect clients and the public while the interim suspension is in place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirement: file written answer and service
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty (30) days from the date of the Final Order, Respondent's written answer shall be filed with the hearing officer and a copy served on the OED Director in accordance with the Complaint's instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order sets a strict 30-day deadline and service procedure to advance the formal disciplinary proceeding after referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority for action: 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.25
rubrics_metrics.description: The interim suspension and referral rest on the statutory and regulatory authority of 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.25.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites these provisions as the legal basis for suspending practice and initiating formal disciplinary proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order, publish a notice in the Official Gazette (Notice of Interim Suspension), and give notice of the Final Order to appropriate USPTO employees, interested departments/agencies/courts, and appropriate state authorities where the respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order requires public posting (OED Reading Room link) and formal notice to relevant entities to inform stakeholders of the interim suspension and referral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance obligations regarding reinstatement and conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 and, should Respondent seek reinstatement, to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.25(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order references these regulatory provisions as continuing obligations governing conduct during suspension and conditions/process for any future reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for interim suspension: protection of the public and public confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Imposition of an interim suspension while the disciplinary complaint is pending is appropriate to 'protect the public and maintain public confidence in those registered to practice before the USPTO.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order ties the justification for interim suspension to protecting clients and preserving trust in the patent bar, particularly where a conviction is 'consistent with having extremely poor judgment and an inclination to exploit persons ... vulnerable or less sophisticated.'
